answers.filer: PJM Transmission Owners (filed by PECO Energy Company and PJM)
answers.point: Large Load customers would make a minimum contribution to transmission revenue requirements, backed by shortfall payments and financial security.
answers.quote: to make a minimum contribution towards transmission owners’ revenue requirements, along with a shortfall payment and crediting mechanism and financial security obligations

answers.filer: PJM Transmission Owners (filed by PECO Energy Company and PJM)
answers.point: Upgrade costs from Fast Energization go to the zones with large loads for 15 years, then to regional allocation.
answers.quote: this allocation methodology will apply to each portfolio of IRRs identified through PJM’s Fast Energization Process for 15 years

answers.filer: PJM Transmission Owners (filed by PECO Energy Company and PJM)
answers.point: Rates for the three new transmission services largely repeat those FERC approved in the co-location order.
answers.quote: The rates for these services are largely identical to those proposed by the PJM Transmission Owners and approved by the Commission in the Co-Located Load Paper Hearing Order

answers.point: PJM files in answer to FERC's preliminary finding that its tariff lacks operating requirements for large loads.
answers.quote: that PJM’s Tariff appears to be unjust and unreasonable because it lacks provisions addressing ongoing operational requirements for transmission customers taking transmission service on behalf of large loads.

answers.point: Generator interconnection requests and large-load service requests would be studied together in one 12-month process.
answers.quote: which will study together New Service Requests, including Generation Interconnection Requests, and requests from Eligible Customers seeking transmission service on behalf of Eligible Load

answers.point: PJM says the new process should take half the time of today's cycle process.
answers.quote: The process will take half the time of the Cycle process.

answers.point: Customers with retail behind-the-meter generation could net no more than 50 MW of it from their load, as the co-location order directed.
answers.quote: PJM is proposing revisions to Part III, section 34.2 and Schedule 8 of the RAA to implement the 50 MW netting limit.

answers.point: Interim NITS would let large and co-located loads use spare capacity on an interruptible basis.
answers.quote: Interim NITS is a transmission service that allows Eligible Customers serving Eligible Load or Large Load to utilize head room on the system as-available on an interruptible basis

answers.point: PJM's Fast Energization Process studies transmission service and generator interconnection requests together to serve electrically proximate load and generation.
answers.quote: to optimize the Transmission System and yield efficiencies for electrically proximate load and generation

answers.point: PJM's own table maps the order's generator-interconnection concern to a single cycle that studies generation and load together.
answers.quote: Generation and load studied together in one Cycle; IRRs optimized for the whole cohort; interim deliverability schedules

answers.point: Customers asking for service for a Large Load must sign a Transmission Owner Cost Recovery Agreement to enter the process, and developers post readiness deposits in full.
answers.quote: The Fast Energization Process requires Eligible Customers seeking service on behalf of Large Loads to enter into a Transmission Owner Cost Recovery Agreement as a condition of entering the process

answers.point: PJM would post upgrade drivers and capital costs in one searchable place on its website.
answers.quote: PJM will post the required system topology, the drivers of the need for the IRRs, and their capital costs on pjm.com in a single, accessible, and searchable location

answers.point: A customer taking the firm contract demand service would be curtailed on the same footing as network and firm point-to-point service.
answers.quote: FCD Transmission Service will be treated as equivalent to NITS and Firm Point-to-Point Transmission Services for purposes of Curtailment.

answers.filer: Midcontinent Independent System Operator and Inc. and the MISO Transmission Owners
answers.point: A new Large Load Project Review would study every large-load service request, with deposits and milestones to deter speculative ones.
answers.quote: The LLPR also includes deposits, project milestones, and other safeguards designed to discourage speculative Large Load requests.

answers.filer: Midcontinent Independent System Operator and Inc. and the MISO Transmission Owners
answers.point: Large-load customers would bear the cost of the upgrades built for them through cost recovery agreements.
answers.quote: designed to ensure that the costs incurred to provide Transmission Service to Large Load Transmission Customers, including the costs of Large Load Upgrades (defined herein), are born by such customers

answers.filer: Midcontinent Independent System Operator and Inc. and the MISO Transmission Owners
answers.point: MISO would publish the location and estimated costs of large loads on a dashboard.
answers.quote: The results of the LLPR periodically will be published to provide transparency into the location and estimated costs associated with Large Load facilities in the MISO region

answers.filer: Midcontinent Independent System Operator and Inc. and the MISO Transmission Owners
answers.point: Two new services, Firm Service Step Up and Interim NITS, would let customers take service in stages as they build out.
answers.quote: The new Transmission Services available to Large Loads include Firm Service Step Up and Interim Non-Firm NITS service.

answers.filer: Midcontinent Independent System Operator and Inc. and the MISO Transmission Owners
answers.point: Loads of 200 MW or more partnered with a generator for at least 15 years go through the resource study instead.
answers.quote: If the Large Load is greater than or equal to 200 MW and has formally partnered with a generator for a minimum of fifteen years, then the applicants will go through the LARS study process.

answers.filer: Midcontinent Independent System Operator and Inc. and the MISO Transmission Owners
answers.point: Transmission owners' study reports filed with a large-load application must say which alternative transmission technologies were considered and what was decided.
answers.quote: requires Large Load Transmission Customers to include with their LLLPR Application the applicable Transmission Owner’s Interconnection Study Report, specifically identifying what ATTs and GETs were considered

answers.filer: Midcontinent Independent System Operator and Inc. and the MISO Transmission Owners
answers.point: A load that wants to co-locate with generation must first have an interconnection agreement, such as a zero-injection agreement, in place for the generator.
answers.quote: if the applicants are looking to co-locate the Load with the generation, then they will need to ensure that an appropriate Interconnection Agreement e.g. “ZGIA” has already been executed for the generator

answers.filer: Midcontinent Independent System Operator and Inc. and the MISO Transmission Owners
answers.point: Paired generation can ask for up to 150 percent of the load's peak demand and must sit in the same resource zone.
answers.quote: limits the requested interconnection service to 150 percent of the paired load’s peak demand, and requires the load and generation to be located in the same Local Resource Zone

answers.point: GRITS is a permanent firm and non-firm contract demand service for large loads that can cut their withdrawals.
answers.quote: GRITS provides a permanent firm and non-firm contract demand-based, Transmission Service option for Large Loads willing and able to limit their withdrawals under specified price and reliability conditions.

answers.point: Example: a 500 MW load could take 200 MW firm and 300 MW non-firm.
answers.quote: a Large Load Transmission Customer representing a Large Load of 500 MW may desire to only take 200 MW of firm transmission service

answers.point: GRITS is not limited to loads served by a co-located generator.
answers.quote: is not limited to Large Load being served by a co-located generator

answers.point: A customer must request GRITS through the Large Load Project Review, the same study route as other large-load service.
answers.quote: A Large Load Transmission Customer must request GRITS through the applicable LLPR process

answers.point: A large load is a single site of 50 MW or more.
answers.quote: and that has a peak load of 50 MW or greater.

answers.point: Deposits, security and cost recovery are left to each transmission owner's tariff.
answers.quote: the PTOs will implement just and reasonable deposit, security, reimbursement, and cost-recovery provisions in their own tariffs

answers.point: Generator interconnection customers must disclose plans to serve co-located load.
answers.quote: requires generator interconnection customers to disclose plans to serve co- located load

answers.point: FILI would let flexible loads energize before network upgrades are finished.
answers.quote: The CAISO’s Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (FILI) can permit earlier energization while network upgrades are pending

answers.point: A permanent flexible service is left for later work.
answers.quote: with additional work planned on permanent flexibility and other emerging configurations

answers.point: CAISO does not require large loads to bring their own generation, and says it will not copy generation-linked mechanisms used in other regions.
answers.quote: This distinction also explains why the CAISO does not propose to replicate generation-linked mechanisms developed or proposed in other ISO/RTO regions.

answers.point: CAISO says a load sitting near generation does not by itself reduce transmission needs or resource adequacy obligations.
answers.quote: physical proximity between load and generation does not guarantee reduced transmission requirements or resource adequacy obligations

answers.point: Large loads with backup or non-exporting behind-the-meter generation would be handled under local retail interconnection rules, not CAISO's resource process.
answers.quote: These will include large loads with back-up generation only to be used during outages or islanding, and large loads with non-exporting behind-the-meter generation.

answers.point: CAISO says it will set out the alternatives, including alternative transmission technologies, considered for each preferred transmission solution.
answers.quote: The CAISO will continue to set out the alternatives that were considered in the selection of all preferred transmission solutions, whether ATTs or other more conventional solutions

answers.point: CAISO agrees to post cost data for large-load network upgrades on its website in a searchable format.
answers.quote: The CAISO agrees that cost data should be transparent and can be provided on the CAISO website in a searchable format.

answers.point: Study, planning, interconnection and expansion requests would be governed by SDG&E's tariff.
answers.quote: any study, planning, interconnection or expansion requests related to Citizens Sunrise’s interest in the Sunrise Project will be governed by the relevant provisions of the SDG&E TO Tariff

answers.point: New language in Sections 8, 9 and 10 repeats the point, one section at a time.
answers.quote: Added new language to Section 10, Interconnection Process, to confirm that all conduct that falls under Section 10 will be governed by SDG&E’s TO Tariff

answers.point: Study, planning, interconnection and expansion requests would be governed by SDG&E's tariff.
answers.quote: any study, planning, interconnection or expansion requests related to Citizens Sycamore’s interest in the Sycamore Project will be governed by the relevant provisions of the SDG&E TO Tariff

answers.point: New language in Sections 8, 9 and 10 repeats the point, one section at a time.
answers.quote: Added new language to Section 10, Interconnection Process, to confirm that all conduct that falls under Section 10 will be governed by SDG&E’s TO Tariff

answers.point: Study, planning, interconnection and expansion requests would be governed by IID's policies and open access tariff.
answers.quote: will be governed by the relevant provisions and policies of IID, including its Open Access Transmission Tariff

answers.point: Its original tariff was thinner than the other Citizens tariffs, so these revisions expand it to match them.
answers.quote: revisions that would expand these sections so that they mirror those of the other Citizens Energy Corporation PTOs

answers.point: SCE takes CAISO's 50 MW definition into its tariff.
answers.quote: SCE proposes to incorporate the CAISO’s definition of “Large Load” into its TO Tariff

answers.point: A new appendix holds the large load interconnection procedures.
answers.quote: SCE proposes to create a new Appendix titled the Large Load Interconnection Procedures (“LLIP”) to augment existing TO Tariff interconnection and cost responsibility sections

answers.point: A request needs a $250,000 study deposit and a readiness deposit of twice that.
answers.quote: an Interconnection Study Deposit of $250,000, a Commercial Readiness Deposit equal to two times the study deposit

answers.point: The same transmission rules apply to SCE's own retail large load customers.
answers.quote: SCE’s LLIP thus applies the same transmission-related requirements to SCE’s own Large Load retail transmission customers as it does to Eligible Customers seeking to interconnect on behalf of Large Loads

answers.point: A 15-year minimum revenue obligation backed by five years of security protects against stranded network upgrade costs.
answers.quote: a 15-year minimum transmission revenue obligation backed by 5 years of security

answers.point: Early termination after service starts costs the customer all remaining required security.
answers.quote: early termination triggers an Exit Fee equal to all remaining required security, including the MARO security, due within 30 Business Days

answers.point: Curtailment terms for the interim service sit in an appendix to the security and reliability agreement.
answers.quote: the conditions and limitations applicable to FILI service, including curtailments, are specified in Appendix E to the TSRA

answers.point: It proposes no new transmission service, deferring to CAISO.
answers.quote: DCRT has not proposed additional or revised transmission services in this filing

answers.point: Its study steps average about 85 days, within the 60 to 90 day range FERC set.
answers.quote: these steps will average roughly 85 calendar days from start to finish, meeting the OSC Order’s target of 60–90 days

answers.point: Its pro forma large load interconnection agreement is modeled on CAISO's generator agreement.
answers.quote: generally modeled on the CAISO’s pro forma Large Generator Interconnection Agreement (“LGIA”)

answers.point: Co-located generation that exports must still go through CAISO's generator process.
answers.quote: Any generating facility that will export energy to the CAISO Controlled Grid, however, must interconnect through the CAISO’s GIDAP and execute a Commission-accepted LGIA

answers.point: The interim service lasts until the identified upgrades reach commercial operation.
answers.quote: a Large Load Interconnection Customer may elect to take FILI Service until the Network Upgrades identified in Appendix A have achieved Commercial Operation

answers.point: Large load facilities are reimbursed for upgrades over $10 million once they reach commercial operation.
answers.quote: Large Load Facilities will be reimbursed for Reimbursable Network Upgrades costing more than $10 million if the Large Load Facility reaches commercial operation

answers.point: PG&E builds the response around a new tariff section for the utilities that buy transmission service for large loads.
answers.quote: primarily through a new Section 10A of its TO Tariff that governs the interconnection of TCLLs to the transmission system on behalf of their Large Load End Users

answers.point: PG&E adopts CAISO's definition of large load.
answers.quote: PG&E proposes to amend its TO Tariff to adopt the CAISO’s proposed definition of Large Load

answers.point: Each application needs a cash study deposit plus per-megawatt security.
answers.quote: The study deposit requirement includes a $500,000 cash deposit and financial security in the amount of $1,000 per MW of requested maximum load

answers.point: Independent loads are studied one at a time. Dependent loads are studied in an annual cluster.
answers.quote: PG&E proposes a Serial Study Process for Electrically Independent Large Loads and a Cluster Study Process for Electrically Dependent Large Loads

answers.point: A cost assurance agreement sets a minimum annual revenue obligation backed by five years of security.
answers.quote: the Cost Assurance Agreement establishes a Minimum Annual Revenue Obligation payable by the TCLL/Large Load End User and a Financial Security requirement equal to five (5) times the Minimum Annual Revenue Obligation

answers.point: Leaving early triggers an exit fee equal to the required security.
answers.quote: the Cost Assurance Agreement provides for an Exit Fee equal to the value of the required Financial Security on the date of termination

answers.point: The interim service is curtailable at all times and only available within limits.
answers.quote: FILLI Interconnection Service is subject to curtailment at all times, and is available only where the Participating TO determines service may be provided within limitations in certain periods under normal operating conditions

answers.point: Its tariff is silent on load interconnection because it does not serve load, so it says no large load provisions are needed.
answers.quote: SunZia Transmission does not directly serve load and, accordingly, there are no provisions in its TO Tariff that address the interconnection of the load to the SunZia Transmission System

answers.point: The only edit confirms the CAISO tariff controls generator and co-located interconnection.
answers.quote: Section 8 of the TO Tariff has been amended to clarify that the CAISO Tariff will continue to control with respect to the interconnection of Generating Units

answers.point: SunZia wants CAISO to start its electrically proximate load work as soon as possible.
answers.quote: SunZia Transmission continues to support the need to apply these enhanced Large Load interconnection procedures to Electrically Proximate Loads

answers.point: Its definition differs from CAISO's wording. It covers a new customer, not an end user.
answers.quote: a new customer, located at a single site behind one or more points of interconnection to the CAISO Controlled Grid, and that has a peak load of 50 MW or greater

answers.point: SDG&E keeps its serial study process, ranked by the date it receives each application.
answers.quote: SDG&E proposes to maintain its current serial study process that accepts and studies each application at any time on a rolling basis, with priority based on the date SDG&E, as the PTO, receives the application

answers.point: It proposes full protection for network upgrade costs.
answers.quote: SDG&E’s proposed 100 percent cost-shift protection for network upgrades

answers.point: Security equals the present value of the upgrades' lifecycle revenue requirement.
answers.quote: security equal to the present value of the forecast lifecycle revenue requirement associated with the network upgrades

answers.point: Security is held until ten years after the upgrades enter service.
answers.quote: maintain security for a period of time beginning with the ECLL’s authorization for SDG&E to begin construction of the network upgrades and ending ten years following the COD of the required network upgrades

answers.point: If the load fails or stops, SDG&E draws all remaining security.
answers.quote: SDG&E will draw all remaining security (effectively, an “exit fee”)

answers.point: Limits on the interim service are set in the study, not from real-time conditions.
answers.quote: SDG&E will establish limits on ECLL grid withdrawals based on studies conducted during the interconnection process, not on near-real-time or real-time operating conditions

answers.point: It says it could not fully align with the other owners in the time available.
answers.quote: given the short timeframe, the complexity of issues involved, and the large number of PTOs, it was not possible to coordinate in perfect lockstep with all other PTOs

answers.point: It requires applicants to disclose other requests for the same large load or its affiliates.
answers.quote: disclosure of any other interconnection requests to the ISO Controlled Grid the applicant has filed on behalf of the same Large Load or any of its affiliate(s)

answers.point: It proposes a coordination process between owners and argues a process favoring load-serving owners' facilities would not be just and reasonable.
answers.quote: A large load interconnection process that favored connecting to load serving entity PTO facilities would not be just and reasonable

answers.point: It files no cost recovery mechanism of its own.
answers.quote: the TO Tariff Revisions do not include a separate pro forma Large Load Interconnection Agreement or cost recovery mechanisms

answers.point: Co-located loads would be studied net of the co-located generation's output.
answers.quote: facilities will be studied based on their expected load on the transmission system, net of the co- located generation’s output that offsets the large load’s energy usage

answers.point: It says curtailment duties for the interim service must be enforceable.
answers.quote: for the FILLI offering to function as intended, curtailment obligations must be enforceable and the chain of authority must be clear

answers.point: It proposes no tariff changes on electrically proximate generation, following CAISO.
answers.quote: Viridon Path 15 does not propose making any changes to its Path 15 Tariff on this issue

answers.point: It adds a process for utilities that buy transmission service on behalf of large loads.
answers.quote: adding a new Section 10A and a new Appendix VI (Large Load Interconnection Procedures (“LLIP”)) to establish an interconnection process for Eligible Customers for Large Load (“ECLLs”)

answers.point: The definition is 50 MW of peak load at a single site.
answers.quote: a Large Load is an End-User located at a single site behind one or more Points of Withdrawal from the CAISO Controlled Grid with a peak load of 50 MW or greater

answers.point: The cost recovery agreement sets a 20-year minimum revenue contribution for each upgrade.
answers.quote: establishes the Eligible Customer’s twenty-year Minimum Transmission Revenue Contribution (“MTRC”) and related payment and security obligations for each Covered Upgrade

answers.point: Ending service early costs the customer all remaining revenue responsibility.
answers.quote: the Eligible Customer owes a lump-sum Termination Fee equal to the Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility

answers.point: Direct security can be reduced by security the large load posted under a retail agreement.
answers.quote: allowing an Eligible Customer to rely on credit support posted by a large load under a retail agreement, direct Operational Security is reduced dollar-for-dollar by Qualifying Retail Security Support

answers.point: Interim curtailable service is curtailed ahead of firm service.
answers.quote: FILI Service is subject to curtailment, including during normal operating conditions, and is curtailed before Firm Interconnection Service

answers.point: It copies CAISO's 50 MW definition of large load.

answers.quote: The definition includes a 50 MW load size which is reasonable for the New England transmission system.

answers.filer: ISO New England Inc. and NEPOOL Participants Committee and the Participating Transmission Owners
answers.point: Interim Contract Demand Service would last up to seven years, or until the required network upgrades are in service if that takes longer.
answers.quote: Interim Contract Demand Service shall be available for a term of no more than seven years, or the length of time required to place the required Large Load Network Upgrades in-service, whichever is longer

answers.filer: ISO New England Inc. and NEPOOL Participants Committee and the Participating Transmission Owners
answers.point: Interim and non-firm service would be re-dispatched when the large load's price exceeds $250/MWh.
answers.quote: all or a portion of a Large Load’s Interim Contract Demand Service and Non-Firm Contract Demand Service will be re-dispatched when the Large Load’s applicable LMP exceeds a Large Load Re-Dispatch Price of $250/MWh.

answers.filer: ISO New England Inc. and NEPOOL Participants Committee and the Participating Transmission Owners
answers.point: Where combined impacts need detailed study, ISO-NE would use reasonable efforts to publish the final system impact study report within 120 days of the preliminary report.
answers.quote: If the Cluster Study and other coordination screening determines that there are combined impacts that need to be studied in detail, then the ISO shall use reasonable efforts consistent with Good Utility Practice to complete the additional coordination analysis (i.e., with the Cluster and other studies) and publish a final Large Load System Impact Study report within 120 days of publishing the preliminary Large Load System Impact Study report.

answers.filer: ISO New England Inc. and NEPOOL Participants Committee and the Participating Transmission Owners
answers.point: ISO-NE proposes a netting threshold of zero MW, which applies only to Large Loads.
answers.quote: the ISO proposes a netting threshold of zero MW (which applies only to Large Loads).

answers.filer: ISO New England Inc. and NEPOOL Participants Committee and the Participating Transmission Owners
answers.point: ISO-NE says injection from a generator one or more substations away from the load would likely not fully flow to that load, which is why it limits proximity.

answers.filer: New York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: Non-firm service would be curtailed when the local price reaches $200 per megawatt-hour.
answers.quote: establish a rule under which Non-Firm Withdrawal Service would be curtailed when the applicable nodal Locational- Based Marginal Price (“LBMP”) for a Large Load reaches $200 MW/h

answers.filer: New York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: The New York transmission owners file a separate two-party cost recovery agreement.
answers.quote: the NYTOs will submit a new two-party pro forma cost recovery agreement to address the cost- shifting issues discussed in the Show Cause Order

answers.filer: New York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: NYISO's study cycle would take about 18 to 24 months, with a 90-day system impact study inside it.
answers.quote: between one year and six months and two years, including a 90-day period for the performance of the System Impact Study

answers.filer: New York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: The new study process includes a description of how alternative transmission technologies will be considered.
answers.quote: (x) describe how alternative transmission technologies will be considered

answers.filer: New York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: NYISO ties paired generation to the same capacity region as the load instead of using the order's electrically proximate test.

answers.filer: New York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: A partner resource serving a large load must be in the same capacity region as that load.
answers.quote: for a Partner Resource Arrangement, the Resource must be located in the same Capacity Region as the given Large Load.

answers.filer: New York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: NYISO adds a co-located load and generator arrangement that lets the load take firm withdrawal service.
answers.quote: Large Loads or portions thereof and an “Associated Resource(s)” that enter into a “Co-Located Arrangement” or “Partner Resource Arrangement” so that the Large Load may be served via some amount of Firm Withdrawal Service

answers.filer: LS Power Grid New York Corporation INew York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: LS Power Grid proposes a company-specific way to recover the cost of upgrades driven by large loads.
answers.quote: a transparent, company-specific mechanism for LS Power Grid to recover the costs of transmission upgrades that are identified as necessary

answers.filer: LS Power Grid New York Corporation INew York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: No upgrade is listed yet, so the filing does not change current rates.
answers.quote: No Large Load-Driven Upgrade is listed in proposed Table 1 as of the requested effective date

answers.filer: LS Power Grid New York Corporation INew York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: An upgrade enters the rate only after a separate section 205 filing adds it to the table.
answers.quote: a Large Load-Driven Upgrade becomes an Eligible Project only after Commission acceptance of a section 205 filing adding it to Table 1

answers.filer: LS Power Grid New York Corporation INew York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: The agreement sets a fixed annual minimum revenue contribution for each covered upgrade.
answers.quote: the CRA establishes a fixed Annual Minimum Transmission Revenue Contribution (“Annual MTRC”)

answers.point: The contribution runs 20 years from the upgrade's in-service date.
answers.quote: MTRC Term begins on the actual Upgrade In-Service Date and ends on the day immediately preceding its twentieth anniversary

answers.filer: LS Power Grid New York Corporation INew York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: Operational security equals all remaining revenue responsibility.
answers.quote: The CRA requires Operational Security equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the nominal Remaining Cumulative Revenue Responsibility

answers.filer: LS Power Grid New York Corporation INew York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: Retail security can offset it dollar for dollar if the customer certifies it is available and enforceable.
answers.quote: the direct Operational Security requirement may be reduced dollar-for-dollar by qualifying retail security support only where the Eligible Customer delivers a current Retail Security Certification

answers.filer: LS Power Grid New York Corporation INew York Independent System Operator, Inc.
answers.point: It calls the termination fee an accelerated contractual charge, not a penalty.
answers.quote: The Termination Fee is an accelerated contractual termination charge, not a penalty

answers.filer: New York Independent System Operator, Inc. and 6 others
answers.point: Each owner recovers all allocated upgrade and facility costs from the large load customer.
answers.quote: recover 100% of the costs of Network Upgrades and Attachment Facilities allocated to a Large Load Customer

answers.filer: New York Independent System Operator, Inc. and 6 others
answers.point: The customer posts security that the owner can draw on if the project is abandoned or the customer defaults.
answers.quote: requires the Large Load Customer to post security for those allocated costs, which the Transmission Owner may draw upon in the event of abandonment of a Large Load project, default, or other specified events

answers.filer: New York Independent System Operator, Inc. and 6 others
answers.point: Non-firm withdrawal service would be limited to thermal and resource adequacy constraints.
answers.quote: limit Non-Firm Withdrawal Service to thermal and resource adequacy constraints

answers.filer: New York Independent System Operator, Inc. and 6 others
answers.point: The owners' agreement for facilities studies sets fixed deposits and a schedule inside NYISO's study timeline.
answers.quote: a pro forma Facilities Study Agreement provides a uniform framework, fixed study deposits, and a defined schedule for the Facilities Studies the Transmission Owners perform under Attachment LL

answers.filer: New York Independent System Operator, Inc. and 6 others
answers.point: The owners add operating requirements for large loads paired with co-located or partner generation.
answers.quote: operating requirements that apply to Large Loads interconnected under the LLIP, including Large Loads that take Non-Firm Transmission Withdrawal Service at a level below their maximum potential withdrawal and Large Loads paired with Co-Located or Partner Resources

study.t: One Fast Energization Process studies load and generator requests together
study.quote: which will study together New Service Requests, including Generation Interconnection Requests, and requests from Eligible Customers seeking transmission service on behalf of Eligible Load

study.t: Studies complete in 12 months, half the time of today's cycle
study.quote: The Fast Energization Process proposes key reforms to the existing process to complete studies in 12 months

study.t: Screening phase of about four months: two rounds of under 60 days each
study.quote: This accelerated Screening Phase will extend for approximately four months, thereby providing two quick rounds of analysis that each take less than 60 days

study.t: Readiness Deposits posted with the application, at risk at Decision Points I and II
study.quote: having Readiness Deposits posted with the Applications and at risk at Decision Points I and II

cost.t: Large loads make a minimum contribution to TO revenue requirements, with shortfall payments and financial security
cost.quote: to make a minimum contribution towards transmission owners’ revenue requirements, along with a shortfall payment and crediting mechanism and financial security obligations

cost.t: Fast Energization upgrade costs go to the large-load zones for 15 years
cost.quote: this allocation methodology will apply to each portfolio of IRRs identified through PJM’s Fast Energization Process for 15 years

cost.t: A Transmission Owner Cost Recovery Agreement is a condition of entering the process
cost.quote: The Fast Energization Process requires Eligible Customers seeking service on behalf of Large Loads to enter into a Transmission Owner Cost Recovery Agreement as a condition of entering the process

cost.t: Upgrade drivers and capital costs posted on pjm.com in one searchable place
cost.quote: PJM will post the required system topology, the drivers of the need for the IRRs, and their capital costs on pjm.com in a single, accessible, and searchable location

colo.t: Netting of behind-the-meter generation capped at 50 MW
colo.quote: PJM is proposing revisions to Part III, section 34.2 and Schedule 8 of the RAA to implement the 50 MW netting limit

colo.t: Rates for the three new services largely those FERC approved in the co-location paper hearing
colo.quote: The rates for these services are largely identical to those proposed by the PJM Transmission Owners and approved by the Commission in the Co-Located Load Paper Hearing Order

flex.t: Adopts the three new transmission services FERC put forward
flex.quote: PJM also proposes implementing the three new transmission services the Commission put forward in a way that will ensure reliability

flex.t: Interim NITS: interruptible use of spare headroom while upgrades are built
flex.quote: Interim NITS is a transmission service that allows Eligible Customers serving Eligible Load or Large Load to utilize head room on the system as-available on an interruptible basis

flex.t: Interim NITS is energy-only, not capacity-backed
flex.quote: Interim NITS is an energy-only service (i.e., it is not capacity backed).

flex.t: Firm Contract Demand service curtailed on par with NITS and firm point-to-point
flex.quote: FCD Transmission Service will be treated as equivalent to NITS and Firm Point-to-Point Transmission Services for purposes of Curtailment.

proximate.t: Generation and load studied together in one cycle; upgrades optimized for the whole cohort
proximate.quote: Generation and load studied together in one Cycle; IRRs optimized for the whole cohort; interim deliverability schedules

proximate.t: Joint study meant to yield efficiencies for electrically proximate load and generation
proximate.quote: to optimize the Transmission System and yield efficiencies for electrically proximate load and generation

study.t: Large Load Project Review (LLPR) for new loads of 50 MW+ or existing loads growing 25 MW+
study.quote: establishes the LLPR process for new loads of 50 MW or more and existing loads increasing by at least 25 MW in the aggregate

study.t: Three study cycles a year; deadlines posted at least 90 days ahead
study.quote: Requires LLPR studies three times in a 365-day period with application deadlines posted at least 90 calendar days in advance.

study.t: Deposits and project milestones to discourage speculative requests
study.quote: The LLPR also includes deposits, project milestones, and other safeguards designed to discourage speculative Large Load requests.

study.t: TO study report must name the alternative transmission technologies and GETs considered
study.quote: requires Large Load Transmission Customers to include with their LLLPR Application the applicable Transmission Owner’s Interconnection Study Report, specifically identifying what ATTs and GETs were considered

cost.t: Large loads bear the cost of Large Load Upgrades through cost recovery agreements
cost.quote: designed to ensure that the costs incurred to provide Transmission Service to Large Load Transmission Customers, including the costs of Large Load Upgrades (defined herein), are born by such customers

cost.t: LLPR results published: location and estimated cost of each large load
cost.quote: The results of the LLPR periodically will be published to provide transparency into the location and estimated costs associated with Large Load facilities in the MISO region

colo.t: Co-located load needs the generator's interconnection agreement (e.g. a ZGIA) executed first
colo.quote: if the applicants are looking to co-locate the Load with the generation, then they will need to ensure that an appropriate Interconnection Agreement e.g. “ZGIA” has already been executed for the generator

colo.t: GRITS contract demand service is not limited to co-located loads
colo.quote: is not limited to Large Load being served by a co-located generator

flex.t: GRITS: permanent firm and non-firm contract demand service for loads that limit withdrawals
flex.quote: GRITS provides a permanent firm and non-firm contract demand-based, Transmission Service option for Large Loads willing and able to limit their withdrawals under specified price and reliability conditions.

flex.t: Example: a 500 MW load takes 200 MW firm, the rest non-firm
flex.quote: a Large Load Transmission Customer representing a Large Load of 500 MW may desire to only take 200 MW of firm transmission service

flex.t: Firm Service Step Up and Interim Non-Firm NITS for staged build-out
flex.quote: The new Transmission Services available to Large Loads include Firm Service Step Up and Interim Non-Firm NITS service.

proximate.t: Loads of 200 MW+ partnered with a generator for 15+ years use the LARS study
proximate.quote: If the Large Load is greater than or equal to 200 MW and has formally partnered with a generator for a minimum of fifteen years, then the applicants will go through the LARS study process.

proximate.t: Paired generation capped at 150% of the load's peak, in the same Local Resource Zone
proximate.quote: limits the requested interconnection service to 150 percent of the paired load’s peak demand, and requires the load and generation to be located in the same Local Resource Zone

study.t: Transmission owners (PTOs) keep studying load requests under their own tariffs
study.quote: the PTOs will continue to govern and study all load interconnection requests pursuant to their tariffs

study.t: CAISO reviews each PTO study against its planning models
study.quote: the CAISO will review PTO load interconnection studies to confirm that study assumptions, load characteristics, and results are consistent with the CAISO’s planning models

study.t: $500,000 cash study deposit plus $1,000 per MW of security
study.quote: The study deposit requirement includes a $500,000 cash deposit and financial security in the amount of $1,000 per MW of requested maximum load

study.t: $250,000 study deposit; readiness deposit of twice that
study.quote: an Interconnection Study Deposit of $250,000, a Commercial Readiness Deposit equal to two times the study deposit

cost.t: Cost allocation set in PTO tariffs, not CAISO's
cost.quote: the CAISO believes it is prudent for cost allocation rules to be set forth in the PTO tariffs rather than the CAISO tariff

cost.t: Network-upgrade cost data posted on CAISO's website, searchable
cost.quote: The CAISO agrees that cost data should be transparent and can be provided on the CAISO website in a searchable format.

cost.t: 15-year minimum revenue obligation backed by 5 years of security
cost.quote: a 15-year minimum transmission revenue obligation backed by 5 years of security

cost.t: Security of 5× the minimum annual revenue obligation
cost.quote: a Financial Security requirement equal to five (5) times the Minimum Annual Revenue Obligation

colo.t: Generator interconnection customers must disclose plans to serve co-located load
colo.quote: requires generator interconnection customers to disclose plans to serve co- located load

colo.t: Backup-only or non-exporting behind-the-meter generation handled under retail rules, not CAISO's
colo.quote: These will include large loads with back-up generation only to be used during outages or islanding, and large loads with non-exporting behind-the-meter generation.

flex.t: Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (FILI): energize before network upgrades finish
flex.quote: The CAISO’s Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (FILI) can permit earlier energization while network upgrades are pending

flex.t: Permanent flexible service left for later work
flex.quote: with additional work planned on permanent flexibility and other emerging configurations

flex.t: Interim service curtailable at all times
flex.quote: FILLI Interconnection Service is subject to curtailment at all times

proximate.t: Does not adopt generation-linked mechanisms from other regions
proximate.quote: does not propose to replicate generation-linked mechanisms developed or proposed in other ISO/RTO regions

proximate.t: Proximity alone does not reduce transmission or resource adequacy needs
proximate.quote: physical proximity between load and generation does not guarantee reduced transmission requirements or resource adequacy obligations

study.quote: The definition includes a 50 MW load size which is reasonable for the New England transmission system.

study.t: $50,000 non-refundable application fee and $150,000 study deposit
study.quote: Initial, non-refundable application fee of $50,000 o Study deposit of $150,000

study.t: Final system impact study report within 120 days of the preliminary one
study.quote: publish a final Large Load System Impact Study report within 120 days of publishing the preliminary Large Load System Impact Study report

cost.t: Large Load Entity pays a Cost Recovery Charge so other customers' rates do not rise
cost.quote: so that there is no increase in transmission rates for other transmission customers caused by the interconnection of the Large Load Facility to the transmission system, the Large Load Entity will pay a Cost Recovery Charge

cost.t: Each load's network upgrades and their costs listed on ISO-NE's website
cost.quote: post on its website, in an easily accessible, searchable and fillable format: (1) a cumulative list reflecting the Large Load Network Upgrades identified for each Large Load

cost.t: A cost recovery agreement alone is insufficient to prevent cost shifting
cost.quote: the PTOs believe that a cost recovery agreement among ISO-NE, the relevant transmission owner, and the Eligible Customer taking transmission service on behalf of large loads is an insufficient guarantor

colo.t: No netting of behind-the-meter generation for wholesale settlement
colo.quote: Effectively, the Tariff Revisions prohibit the netting of a Large Load with Behind-the-Meter Generation for settlement of wholesale services.

colo.t: Netting threshold of zero MW, for large loads only
colo.quote: the ISO proposes a netting threshold of zero MW (which applies only to Large Loads).

flex.t: Interim Contract Demand Service up to 7 years, or until upgrades are in service
flex.quote: Interim Contract Demand Service shall be available for a term of no more than seven years, or the length of time required to place the required Large Load Network Upgrades in-service, whichever is longer

flex.t: Interim and non-firm service re-dispatched when price exceeds $250/MWh
flex.quote: all or a portion of a Large Load’s Interim Contract Demand Service and Non-Firm Contract Demand Service will be re-dispatched when the Large Load’s applicable LMP exceeds a Large Load Re-Dispatch Price of $250/MWh.

proximate.t: Proximate means the same substation and voltage level as the generator, narrower than the order's two substations
proximate.quote: Electrically Proximate Large Load is a configuration where a Large Load’s Point of Delivery is located at (or directly connected radially through dedicated facilities to) the same substation and voltage level as a Generating Facility’s Point of Interconnection

proximate.t: Expedited co-located and proximate generators kept out of the capacity market
proximate.quote: will not be counted towards the region’s capacity for resource adequacy purposes, will not participate in the capacity market

study.t: Large Load threshold: peak of 50 MW or more
study.quote: that has a peak Load of 50 MW or greater connected to the New York State Transmission System

study.t: Study cycle of 18 to 24 months, including a 90-day system impact study
study.quote: between one year and six months and two years, including a 90-day period for the performance of the System Impact Study

study.t: Existing load growing 10 MW+ after a change in use (e.g. to a data center) is restudied
study.quote: a smaller increase in the peak, gross load amount by 10 MW or greater compared to the baseline MW value

study.t: Study Deposits, site control and Readiness Deposits to deter speculative requests
study.quote: The inclusion of Study Deposits, Site Control requirements, and Readiness Deposits will assist in deterring speculative or duplicative submissions

cost.t: TOs recover 100% of allocated network upgrade and attachment facility costs
cost.quote: recover 100% of the costs of Network Upgrades and Attachment Facilities allocated to a Large Load Customer

cost.t: Customer posts security the TO can draw on abandonment or default
cost.quote: requires the Large Load Customer to post security for those allocated costs, which the Transmission Owner may draw upon in the event of abandonment of a Large Load project, default, or other specified events

cost.t: 20-year minimum revenue contribution per upgrade from its in-service date
cost.quote: MTRC Term begins on the actual Upgrade In-Service Date and ends on the day immediately preceding its twentieth anniversary

colo.t: Co-Located or Partner Resource Arrangement lets the load take firm withdrawal service
colo.quote: enter into a “Co-Located Arrangement” or “Partner Resource Arrangement” so that the Large Load may be served via some amount of Firm Withdrawal Service

colo.t: Does not adopt the three services from the PJM co-location order
colo.quote: Part V explains why the NYISO is not proposing to adopt the three new transmission services that the Commission established in the PJM Co-Location Order

flex.t: Firm and Non-Firm Withdrawal Service in place of the PJM services
Non-firm service curtailed when the local price reaches $200/MWh
flex.quote: Non-Firm Withdrawal Service would be curtailed when the applicable nodal Locational- Based Marginal Price (“LBMP”) for a Large Load reaches $200 MW/h

flex.t: Non-firm curtailment limited to thermal and resource adequacy constraints
flex.quote: limit Non-Firm Withdrawal Service to thermal and resource adequacy constraints

proximate.t: Same Capacity Region test in place of the order's electrically proximate test
proximate.quote: use Associated Resource rules tied to NYISO Capacity Regions in lieu of the Show Cause Order’s “electrically proximate resource

proximate.t: A partner resource must sit in the same Capacity Region as the load
proximate.quote: for a Partner Resource Arrangement, the Resource must be located in the same Capacity Region as the given Large Load.
